text: The Patriots' offensive crisis deepened this week in a thoroughly humbling 35-6 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars, with Drake Maye's struggles taking center stage as New England ranks dead last in the NFL at just 9.7 offensive points per game. Maye himself acknowledged the severity of the situation, calling both his own performance and the offense's output "unacceptable" after coughing up three turnovers—two interceptions and a lost fumble—in Sunday's blowout; the film breakdown reveals systemic issues with how the offense is being deployed and how Maye is operating within it, raising serious questions about whether the Patriots are using their young quarterback in a way that sets him up for success. The Jacksonville defense, meanwhile, got contributions from across the roster, while Marcus Jones managed to snag his first interception of the season in a game that offered precious few bright spots for New England. Coach Mike Vrabel addressed the loss in his Monday press conference, though the focus remains squarely on figuring out what has gone so catastrophically wrong so quickly in this young season.
